intro: v0.0.19 is the big build after the v0.0.18 playtest: everything from issues #76-#100, a new title screen, new scenes, Lab Supplies, and the Pokédex banter as a little cutscene. Start a new game. Tick each change once you've seen it, and use the notes box for anything that feels off. One choice is yours this round: portraits or full-body pictures for the banter (see "Your pick" at the end).
save: Save: start a new game (the save layout changed).

items.title: Mareep splash and a new title screen (#12)
items.what: At power-on a little Mareep walks in and sparks, then "A fan project by MudrockNGS". The title is notebook paper with the logo and Slowpoke in a lab coat, worn low so its face and ear show, a sleeve tucked around the front.
items.try: Turn the game on and wait at the title.

items.title: Slowking's notices and welcome
items.what: On a new game, Slowking shows the fan-project notice, a short spoiler-free welcome to the story, and the demo notice.
items.try: New Game; read each page (A turns it).

items.title: Emerald-style map names, first-time item descriptions
items.what: Map names pop up in Emerald's style. An item's description shows only the first time you find it.
items.try: Walk between towns and routes; pick up an item twice.

items.title: Everyone sits for breakfast and tea (#84)
items.what: Breakfast at home and tea at Daisy's are seated, everyone facing the right way.
items.try: Play breakfast and Daisy's scene.

items.title: Jenny walks beside Elm (#83), Cruller joins the cast
items.what: Jenny follows Elm the way Ivy follows you. Jenny's Growlithe is Cruller.
items.try: Watch Elm and Jenny arrive and leave in scenes.

items.title: Route 1 reworked (#85, #88)
items.what: You walk together, there's a song, Elm's catch review is tighter, and something flies over from Viridian.
items.try: Catch a few Pokémon on Route 1 before walking north with the group.

items.title: The lab: Elm and Jenny take on Oak (#86)
items.what: Win or lose against Elm and Jenny, they challenge Oak's two leftover starters (Oak heals them first) and win. Elm pushes his luck; Oak's Lv 50 Pidgeot and Tauros flatten them (watching is optional). Then you and Ivy may battle the starters too (optional, healed first).
items.try: Play the lab scene once winning and once losing; try Yes and No on both questions.

items.title: Slowpoke naps on the empty starter table
items.what: Oak keeps the two starters; the lab's Slowpoke sleeps on the table from then on. Talk to it, to Oak's Pokémon, and (when Daisy visits) to Muffin.
items.try: Visit the lab after the scene.

items.title: Viridian Forest: talks and a Samurai (#9)
items.what: You and Ivy talk after each Bug Catcher; a Samurai waits in the clearing.
items.try: Beat the Bug Catchers; find the Samurai.

items.title: Watch Elm and Jenny take on Brock (#69)
items.what: After the Pewter rematch Elm asks if you want to come. Three rounds, you and Ivy commentating.
items.try: Beat Brock, do the Pewter rematch, say Yes.

items.title: Pokémon out in the world (#64)
items.what: Pallet's Dodrio, Oak's Diglett, a Chansey beside Nurse Joy, the Forest's Pidgeot and Fearow. Talk to them.
items.try: Look around Pallet, the Pokémon Centers and the Forest.

items.title: Dialogue polish
items.what: Oak's Pokémon, his Ranch Pager tutorial, the Rules call, Delia's Rest offer, Oak's rematch haiku. New: Oak's grant and Lab Supplies lines, the aide's PC topic (drafts for you to rework).
items.try: Read the lab scene and talk to the aide.

items.title: The banter is a little cutscene (#5, #4)
items.what: After a catch (or SELECT on an entry): Ivy and you slide in, the speaker hops, the Pokémon cries and hops, its number is stamped on like an ink stamp, a pencil scribble per line, a ! ? or ♪ bubble on some lines. A: next line, B: skip.
items.try: Catch something new; press SELECT on an entry you own.

items.title: Elm and Jenny call in
items.what: For a Pokémon in Elm's or Jenny's starter family, their video-call face pops in for those lines.
items.try: Register a Pokémon from Elm's or Jenny's starter family.

items.title: Your and Ivy's lines in battle (#95, #7)
items.what: When you or Ivy speak in battle, your picture stands over the message box (and hops). Your side shows you and Ivy together; Elm appears in watched battles.
items.try: The Route 22 double against Elm and Jenny.

items.title: Pokédex numbers and the Area page (#77, #20)
items.what: Kanto's 151 in order, then Johto, with national numbers. The Area page matches the wild Pokémon and the time of day.
items.try: Scroll the list; open Area on Pidgey.

items.title: Field Guide in the Start menu (#91)
items.what: Under the Pokédex: what lives where you stand, by day and by night.
items.try: Start > Guide on a route.

items.title: The research grant: reusable things only (#96)
items.what: Oak's grant is every TM and HM and the key items (Bicycle, Ranch Pager, Exp. Share, the rod...). No balls or medicine in the Bag or the PC any more.
items.try: Look in your Bag after the lab.

items.title: Lab Supplies: a free shop on every PC (#98-#100)
items.what: Start > PC (or any PC) > Lab Supplies: every Poké Ball except the Master Ball, medicine and status heals, Repels, X items, held battle items and berries, Rare Candy (stops at the level cap), PP Up/Max and vitamins. Everything shows "Free".
items.try: Take some Poké Balls and a held item.

items.title: Change a Ball (#97)
items.what: The lab aide moves any party Pokémon into the Poké Ball you pick, free.
items.try: Talk to the aide by the bookshelves > Change a Ball.

items.title: The Start menu PC works properly (#79)
items.what: The PC's menus show on the map, no fade to black.
items.try: Start > PC.

items.title: Rename from the Summary (#71)
items.what: Summary > info page > A renames; erase it all and OK to get the species name back.
items.try: Rename a Pokémon, then clear its name.

items.title: Fair starter moves (#87)
items.what: All six starters begin with a Normal move, a status move and an early move of their type.
items.try: Check your starter's moves after the lab.

items.title: Move relearner polish (#89)
items.what: Normal ink, you stay in the list after teaching, and the TM list shows TM numbers.
items.try: Party > Learn Moves > TM Moves; teach two.

items.title: 19 new TMs (#90)
items.what: TMs that repeated a free tutor move now teach new ones. In: TM51-65 Low Kick, Knock Off, Foul Play, Nasty Plot, Agility, Roost, Heat Wave, Mud Shot, Drill Run, Power Gem, Smart Strike, Iron Defense, Body Press, Charge Beam, Grass Knot; TM68 Fire Fang, TM75 Thunder Fang, TM76 Ice Fang, TM77 Pounce. Out (still in Learn Moves > Tutor Moves): Mega Punch, Mega Kick, Swords Dance, Body Slam, Double-Edge, Counter, Seismic Toss, Mimic, Metronome, Soft-Boiled, Dream Eater, Thunder Wave, Explosion, Rock Slide, Substitute, Fire/Thunder/Ice Punch, Icy Wind.
items.try: Open the TM Case and Learn Moves > Tutor Moves.

items.title: Proper case everywhere (#11)
items.what: "Pokémon", "Save", "Pallet Town" instead of ALL CAPS.
items.try: Open menus, read signs.

items.title: Battle boxes in the notebook colours (#92), the engine's type display (#78)
items.what: Battle text and action boxes match the notebook look; the opponent's types display as the engine does.
items.try: Any battle.

items.title: Your own sprites (#93, #80, #28, #24)
items.what: The female player walks as herself; your own sprite on the bike, surfing and using field moves (Ivy steps aside while you ride); the Trainer Card shows your picture.
items.try: Ride the bike, surf, open the Trainer Card.

items.title: Fixed
items.what: Portraits vanishing on a message's last page (#76); the intro call keeping your name after you hang up (#81); the Move Info screen being almost black (#82); Sumac is now Sequoia (#94).
items.try: Play through a few scenes; press L in battle for Move Info.

items.title: The dex banter: portraits (left) or full-body (right)
items.what: Portraits are the default (Claude's pick: the faces read clearly at GBA size; the full-body pictures are about 20 pixels wide). Debug > Scripts > 13 switches the look so you can compare in game. Tell us which you prefer in the notes.
items.try: Start > Debug > Scripts > 13, then replay a banter with SELECT; 13 again switches back.

items.title: Battle lines: portraits (left) or full-body (right)
items.what: The same switch changes the picture over the battle message box.
items.try: Switch the look, then the Route 22 double.
